question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
5 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 \cos{(x )}=4 y \sin{(x )} + 4\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}5 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 \cos{(x )}=4 y \sin{(x )} + 4 \\ 5 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 4 y \sin{(x )}=2 \cos{(x )} + 4 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- \frac{4 \sin{(x )}}{5})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{\frac{2 \cos{(x )}}{5} + \frac{4}{5}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- \frac{4 \sin{(x )}}{5}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{2 \cos{(x )}}{5} + \frac{4}{5}.$
